data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A decentralized network is more resilient to correlated failure if its operators are independently incentivized to maintain divergent operational practices, creating emergent diversity that a large service's internal alignment pressures eliminate.","counterconditions":[{"case":"Operators are incentivized to conform to the same external standard (e.g., a dominant cloud provider's best practices)","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The large service enforces internal diversity deliberately","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"Operational diversity is too small to prevent failure","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"A large service's internal coordination (e.g., standardization on tooling, centralized configuration management) is efficient but creates correlated failure modes because uniform configurations propagate errors uniformly. Decentralized operators lack this alignment and thus maintain diverse, often inefficient, operational practices. This diversity is an emergent causal barrier: because there is no single configuration management system, a configuration error cannot propagate across the network.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
